1.title: The Business Case Practice in Context
1.text: Welcome to Module three: The Business Case Practice in Context. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. three point one.one Apply the business case practice: business case, benefits management approach, sustainability management approach, project brief, areas of focus of the key roles, effective management and techniques. three point one.two analyze whether an approach is effective and fit for purpose, considering the principles, the techniques and tailoring. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (fifty-one percent). Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: Purpose and the principles it serves
1.text: Purpose and the principles it serves. The business case practice judges whether the project is, and stays, desirable (benefits outweigh costs, risks and dis-benefits), viable (it can be delivered and the benefits realized) and achievable (within its constraints). It supports every decision about continuing to invest.

1.title: Purpose and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose and the principles it serves. The figure shows this: The business case practice: reasons, options, benefits, costs and risks checked at every decision point.

1.title: Purpose and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose and the principles it serves. The main principle is ensure continued business justification. The practice also serves manage by stages (review at each stage end), manage by exception (a benefits tolerance), focus on products (each product contributes to a benefit), learn from experience and tailor. In the Official Book, products are in five point five, roles in Table five point one, management and techniques in five point two and five point three, and tailoring in five point seven.

1.title: The management products
1.text: The management products. Project brief. Starts the project: terms of reference and the outline business case, so the board can decide whether to initiate. Business case. The justification: reasons, options, benefits, dis-benefits, costs, risks and timescale; built in initiation, updated at each stage end. Benefits management approach (P I D). How benefits are identified, measured, owned and reviewed, including after the project. Sustainability management approach (P I D). How the project handles environmental, social and economic sustainability targets and tracks them.

1.title: The management products, continued
1.text: The management products. An output is what is delivered; an outcome is the change when people use it; a benefit is a measurable improvement seen as positive; a dis-benefit is a measurable decline seen as negative. Benefits arrive after delivery, through use. Exam tip: The outline business case is in the project brief; the detailed one is built in initiation. The approaches sit in the P I D. If an option puts the benefits management approach in the project log, it is wrong.

1.title: The key roles
1.text: The key roles. Corporate or programme management. Sets the mandate and the project tolerances; decides when they are threatened. Executive. Owns the business case and is accountable for it; keeps the project worth doing. Senior user. Specifies the benefits users expect and ensures use of the products delivers them. Senior supplier. Ensures the supplier's costs and capability support a viable case.

1.title: The key roles, continued
1.text: The key roles. Project manager. Prepares and maintains the case for the executive; assesses the effect of risks, issues and changes on it. Project assurance. Independently checks that the case is sound, meets corporate standards and still holds. Project board. Approves the case and decides at each stage end whether to continue. Check Table five point one in the book when two roles seem to fit.

1.title: Effective management and techniques
1.text: Effective management and techniques. Develop. Outline case in the brief; detailed case in initiation, with options, costs, benefits, risks and timescale. Verify. Assurance and the board test that the case is sound and the project justified. Maintain. Updated at every stage end and whenever a risk, issue or change could affect it. Confirm. After delivery, benefits reviews check whether the benefits were realized. Options and investment appraisal: compare doing nothing, doing the minimum and the proposed solution on cost, benefit, risk and time.

1.title: Effective management and techniques, continued
1.text: Effective management and techniques. Benefit profile: for each benefit, the measure, the baseline today, the target, the owner and when it will be measured. Do the same for dis-benefits. Alignment: each product should contribute to a benefit; a product that does not is a candidate to remove. Tolerances: a benefits tolerance says how far forecast benefits may fall before the matter goes up; the project-level limits come from corporate level. Sustainability: weigh environmental, social and economic effects in the case.

1.title: Effective management and techniques, continued
1.text: Effective management and techniques. Project Harbor example: permit processing time falls from five working days to one; the baseline is measured now, Tomas Reyes owns the benefit, and it is measured three months after rollout. Exam tip: The decision looks forward. Money already spent is no reason to continue; only the remaining costs, benefits and risks count.

1.title: Judging a scenario
1.text: Judging a scenario. Decisions. Effective: Case checked at initiation, every stage end and every major change. Red flag: Looked at once, then ignored. Principle: Continued business justification. Benefits. Effective: Measure, baseline, target and owner for each; review planned. Red flag: Vague ("better service"); no owner. Principle: Continued business justification. Tolerance. Effective: Benefits tolerance set; forecast breach escalated. Red flag: Manager hopes benefits will recover. Principle: Manage by exception.

1.title: Judging a scenario, continued
1.text: Judging a scenario. Sustainability. Effective: In the case and tracked in the approach. Red flag: An afterthought or only the supplier's concern. Principle: Tailor. Viability lost. Effective: Raised at once with options. Red flag: Hidden, or the case rewritten to look viable. Principle: Manage by exception. Ownership. Effective: Executive owns; project manager maintains. Red flag: Project manager approves their own case. Principle: Define roles.

1.title: Judging a scenario, continued
1.text: Judging a scenario. When the case is no longer viable: the project manager raises it at once, with the impact and the options (an exception report if tolerances are forecast to be exceeded). The project board decides: continue with a revised plan or case, or stop. A premature close is a good outcome compared with continuing a project that no longer pays. If project tolerances or the mandate are affected, corporate or programme management decides. The project manager never stops or continues the project alone. Tailoring.

2.title: Judging a scenario, continued
2.text: Judging a scenario. Small project: a one-page case and a short benefits table, but it still exists and is still reviewed. Agile or incremental delivery: benefits arrive release by release; measure early and review the case at each stage end. Multi-party: the project's case is the customer's. A supplier's own commercial interest is handled through the commercial management approach, not by rewriting the case. Sustainability-driven: sustainability targets become measured benefits, with more detail in the sustainability approach. Exam tip: If the project manager sees the case failing, escalate at once. The project manager neither decides alone nor waits for the stage end.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. At the end of the build stage of Project Harbor, the forecast benefit has fallen because the harbor master's office will keep paper permits for large vessels. Sam Okafor reports this in the end stage report for the board. Was this appropriate, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Yes, because the board reviews the business case at each stage end. Ensure continued business justification means the board checks the business case at every stage end, and benefit changes are part of that check.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Midway through the pilot stage of Project Harbor, a national regulator announces one permit system that will replace Brightwater's own, so the business case is no longer viable. What should Sam Okafor do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Report it to the board at once, with the impact and the options. The project manager escalates at once so that the board can decide whether to change or stop, because continuing a project that no longer pays breaks continued business justification.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Brightwater's finance rules require an independent check that the Project Harbor business case meets corporate standards before the board approves it. Who should carry out this check? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Aisha Bello, who provides project assurance for the board. Independent checking of the business case is a project assurance focus, and the project manager, support and a team manager are not independent of the work.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Tomas Reyes asks which Project Harbor document will say how, when and by whom the cut in permit processing time will be measured after go-live. Which management product holds this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The benefits management approach. The benefits management approach sets out how benefits are measured, who owns them and when they are reviewed.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Brightwater's board sets a target to cut printed paper use by ninety percent. Sam records the target, its measure and its owner in the sustainability management approach and in the business case. Was this appropriate, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Yes, because targets that support the justification belong in both. Sustainability is part of the business justification, so a target that supports it belongs in the business case and in the sustainability management approach that says how it is measured.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. The Project Harbor board forecasts that extra investment would exceed the project cost tolerance set by Brightwater's corporate level, though the business case still holds. Who must decide whether to approve the extra funding? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Corporate level, which set the project tolerances for the board. Manage by exception means that a forecast breach of the project tolerances goes to the level that set them, because the board's authority ends at those limits.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What three questions does the business case answer? Answer: Is the project desirable, viable and achievable? Question two. What are the four steps of the business case lifecycle? Answer: Develop, verify, maintain and confirm. Question three. Where does the outline business case live? Answer: In the project brief.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which approach says how benefits will be measured and by whom? Answer: The benefits management approach, part of the P I D. Question five. Who owns the business case? Answer: The executive. Question six. When must the business case be reviewed? Answer: At every decision point: each stage end and whenever an event could affect it.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: judge desirable, viable and achievable; support decisions to keep investing. Products: project brief (outline case), business case, benefits and sustainability management approaches (P I D). Roles: executive owns; project manager maintains; assurance checks independently; board approves. Lifecycle: develop, verify, maintain, confirm. Techniques: options appraisal, benefit profile, alignment of products, benefits tolerance, sustainability. Not viable: escalate at once; board decides; corporate level if project tolerances are affected. Tailoring: small means short, never absent; agile means release-by-release benefits.
